factual_methodology.summary: Official Treasury 7–8 October daily yields and Federal Reserve September FOMC minutes support core claims; auction details, same-day European and Brazilian market closes are backed by dated market reporting. Price observations are not conflated with auction clearing yields.

novelty.summary: Unlike 7 October's pending auction and minutes, 8 October evaluates the observed 30-year auction demand, post-auction yield reprieve, Fed's AI infrastructure debt channel and Brazilian recovery.

editorial_publication_readiness.summary: Separates market price levels from mechanism and inference, includes falsifiers, a distinct information cutoff and no trading advice.

contextual_depth.summary: Explains sovereign versus private duration absorption, refined-energy transmission, ECB/French sovereign differentiation and Brazil's sector-versus-fiscal channels.

visual_evidence_readiness.signature: 1 evidence table + 2 unit-consistent charts + 1 causal flow + 1 regional transmission map per locale
visual_evidence_readiness.summary: EN and PT-BR have matching chart scales and regional/causal semantics; official Treasury 7/8 October benchmark pairs use identical units and European 10-year yields are on a shared percent scale.
visual_evidence_readiness.limitations: European and oil observations are reported market session values, not Treasury's official par curve. Brazil closing levels are contemporaneous reported prices.

contrary_evidence: A strong auction can be temporary demand at exceptionally high yields rather than a durable yield ceiling.
Longer-term Treasury yields can rise again if energy and fiscal supply overwhelm demand.
Some of AI infrastructure investment could raise productivity and future supply, tempering inflation effects.
Brazil equity rebounds can be sector composition rather than evidence of a new political-fiscal regime.
limitations: Intraday oil and European sovereign levels depend on quotation time and provider.
Auction high yield and par constant-maturity yield are different instruments and measurement constructions.
The FOMC minutes record participants' September assessments, not an 8 October decision.
Market reactions to Brazil's election are not a causal estimate of eventual fiscal policy.
notes: Reviewed bilingual daily macro 8 October 2026: primary-source facts and same-day market references checked; controlled taxonomy, title, source parity and visual floor inspected; medium confidence because some cross-market observations are non-official session reports.

en.title: Global Macro — strong Treasury demand interrupts the yield spike, while oil and AI borrowing keep the inflation constraint alive
en.deck: The U.S. 30-year auction cleared at 5.618% with 2.54-times cover; benchmark yields fell from Wednesday's close even as Brent stayed above $100 and the Fed exposed a new competition for long-term capital.
en.regime: Strong 30-year auction demand brought 10-year and 30-year Treasury closing yields below 7 October even as oil and private AI-related capital demand sustained inflation and financing pressure.
en.key_risk: Elevated energy costs and competition for long-term funds can overwhelm the relief from one well-received sovereign auction.

pt-BR.deck: Leilão americano de 30 anos saiu a 5,618%, com demanda 2,54 vezes a oferta; juros de referência recuaram frente a quarta-feira, embora o Brent siga acima de US$ 100 e a ata do Fed revele competição adicional por capital de longo prazo.

pt-BR.key_risk: Energia cara e concorrência por financiamento de longo prazo podem superar o alívio temporário de um leilão soberano bem recebido.
